meta.title: Rigetti Computing (RGTI): CEO Subodh Kulkarni's Race to Practical Quantum Advantage — Vertically Integrated Superconducting QPUs, a $589 Million Cash War Chest, and the 1,000-Qubit Threshold
meta.abstract: Rigetti Computing, Inc. (Nasdaq: RGTI) is the United States' sole publicly traded, vertically integrated superconducting quantum computing pure-play, designing, fabricating, and operating quantum processing units (QPUs) from its proprietary Fab-1 facility in Fremont, California. Founded in July 2013 by Chad Rigetti — a Yale-trained physicist who spent formative years at IBM Research — the company went public in March 2022 via a SPAC merger with Supernova Partners Acquisition Company II at an implied enterprise value of approximately $1.5 billion. Under President and CEO Dr. Subodh Kulkarni, who joined in December 2022 following a career arc through 3M, IBM, Imation, and CyberOptics, Rigetti has pivoted from a research-services model toward hardware commercialization anchored by three strategic narratives. First, the Novera QPU commercialization program — launched December 2023 — positions Rigetti as the only company selling on-premises superconducting QPUs to government labs, national computing centers, and research organizations. Second, the February 2025 strategic collaboration with Quanta Computer (combined $200-million-plus, five-year commitment) creates a Taiwanese manufacturing and distribution bridge aimed at scaling superconducting systems toward enterprise deployments. Third, a dual-geography infrastructure strategy — anchored by a March 2026 U.S. Department of Commerce letter of intent for up to $100 million in R&D funding and a concurrent $100 million UK investment commitment targeting a greater-than-1,000-qubit system — positions Rigetti as a geopolitically significant vendor as governments race to secure domestic quantum supply chains. Full-year 2025 revenue was $7.1 million with a non-GAAP operating loss of $50.5 million; however, Q1 2026 revenue of $4.4 million represented 193 percent year-over-year growth, signaling the first inflection of hardware order conversion. With $569 million in cash and no debt as of March 31, 2026, and a market capitalization of approximately $8.8 billion, Rigetti trades at a speculative premium on the thesis that superconducting gate speed — up to 10,000 times faster than trapped-ion alternatives — will underpin the first commercially meaningful quantum advantage demonstrations.

chapters.title: Quantum at the Inflection: Rigetti Computing's Strategic Position as of May 2026
chapters.body:
## The Inflection Arrives on Schedule

On May 11, 2026, Rigetti Computing reported first-quarter results that, for the first time in the company's public life, looked less like a research grant ledger and more like the opening movement of a commercial hardware cycle. Revenue of $4.4 million grew 193 percent year-over-year — the highest growth rate Rigetti had ever posted as a public company — driven by ~~partial milestone recognition on Novera QPU shipments and early bookings against the $8.4 million purchase order from India's Centre for Development of Advanced Computing~~ ==higher Novera system and related product sales, including a shipment to the University of Saskatchewan==. The balance sheet carried $569 million in cash and investments against zero long-term debt. Whatever else the quantum computing sector is, Rigetti entered its 2026 strategic phase with the capital and the early commercial proof-of-concept to make a credible case that the long-awaited inflection had finally arrived.

That inflection had been conspicuously absent in the three prior fiscal years. [FY2025 revenue was $7.1 million](https://investors.rigetti.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rigetti-computing-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-yvxoh4p8fn7k), down from $10.8 million in FY2024 and $12.0 million in FY2023 — a declining curve that prompted uncomfortable comparisons with peers and raised legitimate questions about whether government technology-development contracts could ever mature into a recurring commercial business. The Q1 2026 number does not erase that history; it complicates the bearish narrative sufficiently to demand closer analysis.

## What 'Practical Quantum Advantage' Actually Means

Dr. Subodh Kulkarni, who has served as President and Chief Executive Officer since December 2022, has organized the company's public identity around the phrase *practical quantum advantage* — a formulation that carries distinct technical and commercial meanings that are worth separating precisely because they are so frequently collapsed.

Technically, quantum advantage is achieved when a quantum processing unit solves a specific computational problem faster than the best available classical supercomputer running the best available algorithm. That bar is not theoretical; it is empirical, problem-specific, and contested — a quantum system might beat a classical machine on one instance of a sampling problem while losing on every commercially relevant optimization task. Practically, Kulkarni's version of the phrase adds a second condition: a paying customer must choose quantum over classical because it is faster, cheaper, or more capable in a domain the customer actually cares about. That is a harder bar, and it has not yet been cleared by any commercial quantum organization. What Rigetti is arguing — through hardware fidelity roadmaps, on-premises QPU deployments, and government validation contracts — is that its superconducting architecture is on the shortest credible path to clearing it.

## Three Structural Narratives

Three organizing themes run through this dossier, and each merits a brief introduction here.

The first is **vertical integration**. Rigetti designs, fabricates, and operates its own quantum processors — from transmon qubit geometry through cleanroom production at Fab-1 in Fremont, California, through cloud delivery via the proprietary Quantum Cloud Services platform accessible on AWS Braket and Microsoft Azure. That full-stack ownership is structurally unusual and capital-intensive; it is also, the company argues, the only architecture that allows sufficiently rapid iteration on the hardware-software interface to compress the timeline to practical advantage.

The second is the **Quanta Computer partnership**. In February 2025, Rigetti announced a collaboration with the world's largest server manufacturer — a company with approximately $43 billion in annual revenue and distribution relationships with hyperscale data center operators globally — under which both parties committed more than $100 million each over five years to superconducting quantum commercialization. Quanta separately invested $35 million in Rigetti common stock at $11.59 per share. The partnership is a manufacturing and distribution force-multiplier that no other pure-play quantum hardware company currently possesses.

The third is the ~~dual-government investment thesis~~ ==U.S. funding overture paired with a UK deployment commitment==. In ~~March~~ ==May== 2026, Rigetti signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $100 million in ~~R&D funding under national quantum programs~~ ==funding under national quantum programs, with the agreement contemplating an equity stake for the Department in exchange==. Simultaneously, the company announced plans to invest up to $100 million in the United Kingdom over three to four years to deploy a greater-than-1,000-qubit system — its most ambitious scale milestone to date — anchored by an existing 36-qubit deployment at the National Quantum Computing Centre in Didcot. ~~Together, Washington and London have effectively issued a geopolitical endorsement of Rigetti's roadmap.~~ ==Washington's prospective capital commitment and Rigetti's own UK build-out together signal that the company's roadmap is now embedded in two national quantum strategies.==

## The Valuation Gap

Any honest accounting of Rigetti's strategic position must acknowledge the extraordinary gap between current financial reality and market expectations. As of May 22, 2026, [RGTI carried a market capitalization of approximately $8.79 billion](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000110465926058635/rgti-20260511xex99d1.htm) — against a non-GAAP operating loss of $50.5 million for FY2025 and trailing twelve-month revenue that, even inclusive of the strong Q1 2026 print, implies a revenue multiple exceeding 400 times. This is not an earnings story. It is a long-duration option on the superconducting qubit roadmap, priced by a market that is betting the company's technical trajectory materializes into commercial scale somewhere in the 2028–2032 window. That framing is not a criticism; it is a prerequisite for reading anything that follows with appropriate calibration.

## The Road Ahead

The chapters that follow move from context to evidence. The dossier examines Rigetti's quantum hardware architecture and the technical case for its superconducting transmon design; traces the evolution of Fab-1 and the vertical integration thesis; details the Quanta Computer partnership and what it means for distribution economics; analyzes the government contract pipeline across the United States, United Kingdom, and India; profiles Dr. Kulkarni's operating record and management team; dissects the financial structure chapter by chapter; maps the competitive landscape against IBM, Google, IonQ, and Quantinuum; and closes with a scenario analysis of the conditions under which the practical-advantage threshold gets crossed — and what Rigetti's position looks like on either side of that line.

chapters.title: From Quantum Startup to SPAC Listing: Rigetti Computing's Decade of Founding, Pivots, and Public Markets
chapters.body:
## The Physicist Who Wouldn't Wait

Chad Rigetti did not invent the superconducting qubit. That distinction belongs, in large part, to Michel Devoret, the Yale University physicist whose laboratory became one of the world's premier proving grounds for quantum hardware in the early 2000s. But Rigetti trained under Devoret, absorbed his mentor's conviction that superconducting circuits represented the most tractable path toward scalable quantum computation, and left New Haven with a doctorate and a mounting impatience for what came next.

That impatience deepened at IBM Research, where Rigetti spent time working on quantum hardware and encountered the institutional reality of large-organization science: careful, thorough, and inevitably slow. The frustration was not with the quality of the science but with the distance between laboratory demonstration and commercial deployment — a gap that, in Rigetti's judgment, no incumbent was positioned to close aggressively enough. On July 8, 2013, he incorporated Rigetti Computing in the United States, staking the company on a proposition that was then nearly universally considered premature: that a private company could design, fabricate, and commercially operate superconducting quantum processors within a vertically integrated structure, controlling every layer from qubit design through cloud delivery.

## The Y Combinator Years and the First Chip

The company's first institutional validation came in 2014, when Rigetti Computing was accepted into Y Combinator as a so-called "spaceshot" — the accelerator's designation for companies pursuing outcomes so technically ambitious that conventional venture risk models scarcely applied. The same year, the company participated in The Alchemist Accelerator, extending its early network. These were seed-stage endorsements of a thesis rather than a business, but they provided capital, credibility, and the organizational scaffolding to begin serious hardware work.

By February 2016, Rigetti had produced its first quantum processor: a three-qubit chip etched in aluminum circuits on a silicon wafer. The device was rudimentary by subsequent standards, but its existence confirmed that the founding team could translate academic quantum hardware techniques into a fabrication workflow conducted outside a university cleanroom. The company began constructing Fab-1, its dedicated quantum chip fabrication facility in Fremont, California — one of a small number of purpose-built quantum foundries globally, and the asset that would come to define Rigetti's structural differentiation from competitors who outsourced chip production to university facilities or third-party semiconductor fabs. Successive venture rounds through the late 2010s funded the cleanroom buildout, expanded the engineering team, and kept the hardware roadmap advancing.

## Quantum Cloud Services: ~~The First Internet-Accessible QPU~~ ==An Early Internet-Accessible QPU==

The strategic moment that most clearly established Rigetti's commercial identity arrived in 2017 with the launch of Quantum Cloud Services, or QCS. ~~At the time of its introduction, QCS represented something genuinely novel: quantum computers accessible to external users over the public internet. No organization had previously operated a commercial quantum computing cloud platform in this manner.~~ ==QCS made Rigetti's quantum processors accessible to external users over the public internet, joining IBM — which had opened public cloud access to its own quantum hardware in May 2016 — among the earliest commercial cloud-delivered QPU platforms, and standing out as the one built on a vertically integrated stack of in-house designed and fabricated superconducting processors.== The significance was not merely technical. By making QPU access available as a subscription service, Rigetti established itself as a company with a cloud business model — not only a hardware vendor — and began accumulating the developer relationships and usage data that would inform subsequent system design.

QCS also committed the company to a dual identity that would prove both an asset and a complication. As a hardware company, Rigetti competed on qubit count, gate fidelity, and coherence time — metrics defined by physics and engineering. As a cloud services company, it competed on availability, latency, developer tooling, and pricing — metrics defined by software and operations. Sustaining both simultaneously on a startup balance sheet required a capital efficiency that quantum hardware, with its cryogenic infrastructure and cleanroom dependencies, made structurally difficult to achieve.

## The SPAC Transaction and Nasdaq Debut

By 2021, Rigetti had raised substantial venture capital but remained pre-revenue in any commercial sense, its income derived almost entirely from government research contracts. The SPAC route offered a path to the public markets — and to the balance sheet scale — that a conventional IPO process might have foreclosed in a period when quantum computing remained a pre-commercial category.

In October 2021, Rigetti announced a business combination with Supernova Partners Acquisition Company II, then listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker SNII. The implied enterprise valuation was approximately $1.5 billion — a figure that required investors to price not present earnings but a probability-weighted option on a quantum computing market that most analysts placed a decade or more in the future. Shareholders approved the transaction on February 28, 2022. Rigetti Computing began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker RGTI on March 2, 2022, with approximately $261.75 million in gross proceeds from the transaction.

The timing was, in retrospect, unfortunate for the company's early stock performance. The SPAC wave that had lifted dozens of pre-revenue technology companies in 2020 and 2021 was already receding by early 2022, and rising interest rates compressed the speculative premium embedded in long-duration technology valuations with particular severity. RGTI, like most quantum computing equities, fell sharply from its SPAC-era implied valuation in the months following its listing.

~~The transition also brought an immediate leadership rupture. Chad Rigetti, the company's founder and chief executive, departed in March 2022 — the same month the stock began trading publicly. The circumstances of his departure were not detailed in public filings beyond standard disclosure language, but the timing, coincident with the close of the SPAC transaction, signaled that the company's transition from founder-led startup to publicly accountable commercial enterprise would require governance reconfiguration as well as a new capital structure.~~ ==The transition would also reshape company leadership over the months that followed. Chad Rigetti, the company's founder and chief executive, remained at the helm through the SPAC close and the opening months of public trading, with the CEO transition announced later in 2022. The circumstances of his departure were not detailed in public filings beyond standard disclosure language, but the change signaled that the company's evolution from founder-led startup to publicly accountable commercial enterprise would require governance reconfiguration as well as a new capital structure.==

## The Leadership Reset: Kulkarni and the Commercial Pivot

~~The period between Chad Rigetti's March 2022 departure and the end of that year was one of organizational limbo.~~ ==The interval between Chad Rigetti's 2022 departure and the appointment of a permanent successor was one of organizational limbo.== The company operated under interim leadership while the board conducted a search for a chief executive with the commercial and operational credentials that a Nasdaq-listed hardware business required — credentials that differed meaningfully from those of a quantum physicist-entrepreneur.

In December 2022, the board appointed Dr. Subodh Kulkarni as President and Chief Executive Officer. Kulkarni's background traced a trajectory from IIT Mumbai through an MIT doctorate in chemical engineering and early roles at 3M and IBM before arriving at CyberOptics Corporation in 2014, where he served as President and CEO until the company's acquisition by Nordson Corporation in November 2022 — an acquisition that, in closing the day before Kulkarni accepted the Rigetti role, effectively freed him for the transition. At CyberOptics, Kulkarni had built a profitable maker of high-precision sensors and inspection systems for semiconductor and electronics manufacturers: a business with real customers, real margins, and real hardware operations. The signal the board was sending with this appointment was unambiguous — Rigetti needed commercial discipline as urgently as it needed scientific ambition.

The reconstitution of the senior leadership team continued in early 2023. February brought two appointments that reinforced the CyberOptics organizational DNA: Jeffrey Bertelsen as Chief Financial Officer and David Rivas as Chief Technology Officer, both alumni of the same precision-hardware environment Kulkarni had led. The pairing of a commercially proven CFO with a technology officer who understood hardware manufacturing disciplines suggested a deliberate effort to build an executive team aligned on both financial accountability and operational execution. In October 2023, Thomas Iannotti — a former Hewlett-Packard enterprise executive with substantial experience in global technology sales and government programs — was appointed as Independent Board Chair, providing additional governance weight as the company moved toward its first hardware product launches.

## The Product Cadence: From Transition to Commercialization

The leadership reset's first tangible outputs arrived in 2024. January brought Ankaa-2, an 84-qubit system reporting 98% median two-qubit gate fidelity — representing, by Rigetti's own characterization, a 2.5x performance improvement over the prior generation — made available through QCS and subsequently through Amazon Web Services Braket and Microsoft Azure. April 2024 saw the formal launch of the Novera QPU Partner Program, commercializing the 9-qubit on-premises processor that had been introduced in December 2023 and establishing Rigetti's first structured channel for physical hardware sales to research institutions, national laboratories, and defense installations.

December 2024 delivered Ankaa-3, again at 84 qubits but with fidelity metrics that had advanced to 99.0% median iSWAP gate fidelity and 99.5% median fidelity using fSim gates — numbers that began to approach the threshold that quantum error correction researchers conventionally cite as necessary for near-term fault-tolerance experiments. Together, the Ankaa and Novera launches represented the first evidence that Kulkarni's commercial operating model was producing a product cadence: a rhythm of system introductions, customer engagements, and revenue-generating hardware orders that distinguished the post-SPAC Rigetti from its founder-led predecessor.

The twelve years between incorporation and this product cadence compressed a standard industrial narrative — research, fabrication, cloud deployment, leadership professionalization, first commercial hardware sales — into a timeline that quantum computing's fundamental difficulty made, if anything, surprisingly short. Whether that cadence could accelerate fast enough to reach practical quantum advantage before the company's capital reserves required another dilutive equity raise was the question that would define the next phase.

chapters.title: Superconducting Qubits, Fab-1, and the QCS Platform: Rigetti's Integrated Product Architecture
chapters.body:
## The Vertically Integrated Stack

Most quantum computing companies make a strategic concession that Rigetti Computing does not. IBM fabricates its superconducting processors internally but operates at a scale that dwarfs Rigetti in every dimension. IonQ traps individual ytterbium ions in vacuum chambers that require no semiconductor fabrication whatsoever. Quantinuum licenses Honeywell's trapped-ion expertise. The dominant pattern among smaller quantum hardware firms is to outsource chip production — to university cleanrooms, to contract foundries, to academic collaborators — and focus proprietary effort on software, algorithms, or systems integration.

Rigetti's founding premise rejected that model. When Chad Rigetti left IBM Research in 2013 to start the company, he insisted on owning the full stack: qubit design, wafer fabrication, packaging, cryogenic integration, control electronics, firmware, and the cloud software layer that makes QPU cycles accessible to users who have never seen a dilution refrigerator. The result is Fab-1 in Fremont, California — one of a small number of dedicated quantum chip foundries in the world — where Rigetti engineers deposit aluminum superconducting circuits onto silicon wafers using lithography and process chemistry steps that carry deliberate analogies to conventional semiconductor manufacturing. The process borrows from mature planar fabrication techniques: photolithography for circuit patterning, reactive-ion etching for feature definition, and multilayer deposition sequences that must be calibrated to preserve the superconducting coherence properties that make transmon qubits useful in the first place.

The transmon qubit itself — a Josephson-junction-based superconducting circuit whose nonlinear inductance produces the quantized energy levels used to encode quantum information — is an architecture Rigetti has pursued since the company's first three-qubit chip in 2016. Transmons offer operating gate speeds measured in tens of nanoseconds, roughly four orders of magnitude faster than trapped-ion alternatives. That speed advantage carries a coherence tradeoff: superconducting qubits must operate at temperatures near 15 millikelvin, require complex dilution refrigerator infrastructure, and are more susceptible to environmental noise than ion-trap or photonic qubits. The vertically integrated thesis holds that these engineering challenges are solvable through iterative process control — and that owning the fabrication line is the only way to iterate fast enough.

## Novera to Cepheus: A Product Lineage in Four Generations

Rigetti's commercial product portfolio spans roughly thirty months of systematic capability expansion. The Novera QPU, launched in December 2023, was the company's first commercially available on-premises system — a 9-qubit processor priced for research and experimentation rather than production computation. Novera was positioned deliberately at the entry level: small enough that its cryogenic footprint could fit within an existing laboratory cold-finger infrastructure, and priced to reach national quantum centers and defense research laboratories that lacked the procurement budget for full-scale cloud-integrated systems. Sales followed the thesis. ~~The Air Force Research Laboratory received at least two units.~~ ==Disclosed early Novera sales included one unit to the Superconducting Quantum Materials and Systems Center at Fermilab and one to the Air Force Research Laboratory.== Israel's national quantum computing center co-located a Novera alongside Quantum Machines' OPX1000 control system and NVIDIA Grace-Hopper servers — a hybrid classical-quantum integration stack that demonstrated the hardware's compatibility with high-performance computing workflows. A Japanese research institution placed an order in late 2025 with delivery expected in April 2026, extending the product's Asia-Pacific footprint and establishing what Rigetti called a Novera QPU Partner Program in April 2024.

Ankaa-2, released in January 2024, represented a step-change in performance rather than a modest incremental improvement. At 84 qubits and with a reported 98 percent median two-qubit gate fidelity, Ankaa-2 delivered a 2.5 times performance improvement over its predecessor and was made available not only through Rigetti's native [Quantum Cloud Services](https://www.rigetti.com/qcs) platform but also through Amazon Web Services Braket and Microsoft Azure — the company's first systematic integration into the major public cloud marketplaces. The significance of marketplace integration for developer adoption is material: researchers and enterprise exploratory teams who already manage infrastructure on AWS or Azure could access Rigetti QPU cycles within their existing billing and identity management frameworks without establishing a separate QCS account.

Ankaa-3 followed in December 2024 with the same 84-qubit physical architecture but a meaningfully improved fabrication process. The system achieved 99.0 percent median iSWAP gate fidelity and 99.5 percent median fidelity using fSim gates — a two-qubit gate type that Rigetti's tunable-coupler architecture supports with particular efficiency. Both figures cleared the 99 percent threshold that quantum error correction researchers have identified as the entry condition for near-term experiments in surface code and other topological error correction schemes.

Cepheus-1-108Q entered general availability ~~in the first quarter of 2026~~ ==on April 7, 2026== as Rigetti's largest and most architecturally ambitious deployed system. The jump from 84 to 108 qubits was achieved not by extending the monolithic chip design but by implementing a chiplet-based modular approach — interconnecting multiple smaller QPU dies within a single cryogenic package. Cepheus-1-108Q ~~carries 99.5 percent median fidelity with fSim gates~~ ==reported 99.1 percent current median two-qubit gate fidelity at general availability, with 99.5 percent set as a later-2026 performance target,== and is available across QCS, AWS Braket, and Microsoft Azure, as well as in the on-premises form factor that C-DAC ordered for approximately $8.4 million in late 2025.

## Fidelity as the Strategic Metric

The fidelity progression across Rigetti's product generations is not merely a technical footnote — it is the primary evidence base for the company's commercialization thesis. A comparison across the product lineage shows the trajectory clearly:

| System | Qubits | Year | Two-Qubit Gate Fidelity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Early systems (pre-2022) | ≤32 | 2019–2021 | Sub-90% |
| Ankaa-2 | 84 | Jan 2024 | 98% (median) |
| Ankaa-3 | 84 | Dec 2024 | 99.0% iSWAP / 99.5% fSim |
| Cepheus-1-108Q | 108 | ~~Q1 2026~~ ==Apr 2026== | ~~99.5% fSim~~ ==99.1% at GA (99.5% later-2026 target)== |
| Prototype (28ns gate) | — | 2025 | 99.9% |

The prototype demonstration of 99.9 percent two-qubit gate fidelity at 28-nanosecond gate speed is particularly significant. The 99 percent barrier marks the threshold below which quantum error rates accumulate faster than error correction algorithms can suppress them, making fault-tolerant computation impossible regardless of qubit count. Crossing into the high-nines regime opens the experimental space for near-term surface code demonstrations and small-scale logical qubit experiments. The 99.9 percent prototype result suggests Rigetti's process chemistry and device engineering are operating in a regime where the next meaningful threshold — 99.99 percent, the figure IonQ claims for its trapped-ion systems — is a defined engineering target rather than a speculative aspiration.

The comparison to IonQ deserves a careful framing. Trapped-ion systems achieve exceptional gate fidelity in part because ions are intrinsically identical quantum systems with no fabrication-process variation between qubits, and because their long coherence times — measured in seconds rather than milliseconds — allow for more measurement attempts per computation. The tradeoff is gate speed: trapped-ion gates require laser pulse sequences that unfold over microseconds, roughly 100 to 1,000 times slower than transmon gates. Rigetti's 28-nanosecond two-qubit gate speed, if the 99.9 percent fidelity can be replicated at scale, would represent a system that approaches IonQ's accuracy threshold while maintaining a raw throughput advantage that matters for algorithms requiring deep circuit depth.

## Chiplet Architecture and the Path to 1,000 Qubits

Rigetti's decision to pursue a chiplet-based modular architecture for Cepheus rather than continuing to scale monolithic QPU dies reflects an engineering constraint familiar to conventional semiconductor designers. Larger monolithic chips accumulate yield loss at an exponential rate as feature count grows — each fabrication defect that falls on or near a qubit can degrade an entire processor. By fabricating smaller, higher-yield sub-chips and interconnecting them within a cryogenic module, the chiplet approach isolates defect risk within individual tiles rather than allowing it to propagate across an entire processor. The challenge is engineering the inter-chip interconnects to preserve coherence across the boundary — a microwave photonics problem that Rigetti's in-house packaging and cryogenic integration teams are responsible for solving.

The roadmap implications become clear in the context of Rigetti's March 2026 announcement that it planned to invest up to $100 million in the United Kingdom over the following three to four years to deploy a greater-than-1,000-qubit system — the company's first major quantum computing facility outside the United States. A 1,000-qubit system achieved via chiplet interconnection of ten-times-108-qubit tiles would require roughly ten production-quality Cepheus-class dies wired together in a cryogenic package with inter-chip fidelities comparable to intra-chip performance. Whether that engineering challenge has been solved remains the defining technical question of Rigetti's mid-decade roadmap.

## QCS, Cloud Marketplaces, and the Quantum Foundry Revenue Layer

Rigetti's commercial access model is structured across four distinct channels that collectively define its addressable market. The Quantum Cloud Services platform, operating since 2017 as ~~the first~~ ==an early== internet-accessible quantum computing service ==(IBM had opened public cloud access to its superconducting hardware in May 2016)==, provides direct subscription and pay-per-use access to QPU cycles with queue-based scheduling and Python-accessible programming through the pyQuil SDK and Quil instruction set. AWS Braket and Microsoft Azure integrations constitute the second and third channels — marketplace access for users embedded in existing cloud enterprise agreements. The fourth channel, Quantum Foundry services, is structurally distinct: rather than selling QPU cycles, Rigetti licenses its fabrication process knowledge and produces custom processors for external partners. This positions Rigetti not only as a quantum computing service provider but as a foundry-of-record for organizations that want proprietary superconducting QPU designs without building cleanroom infrastructure of their own.

## The Quanta Computer Manufacturing Multiplier

The February 2025 strategic collaboration with Quanta Computer — the world's leading server and notebook manufacturer, with approximately $43 billion in annual revenue — addresses a constraint that Rigetti's Fab-1 alone cannot resolve: the ability to manufacture, integrate, and deliver cryogenic quantum computing systems at the volume and geographic distribution required for enterprise and national infrastructure deployments. Fab-1 produces QPU chips; it does not produce the dilution refrigerators, control rack systems, and cryogenic wiring harnesses that constitute the full on-premises quantum system a customer like C-DAC actually installs. Quanta's server manufacturing infrastructure handles integration complexity at production scale — a capability it has developed across decades of high-density rack computing for hyperscale data centers. Under the agreement, both parties committed to investing more than $100 million each over five years, with Quanta separately investing $35 million through a direct equity purchase. If the partnership converts into a functioning go-to-market channel, Rigetti's deliverable capacity for on-premises QPU systems could scale well beyond what its existing Fremont operations support — addressing what would otherwise become the binding constraint as hardware contract backlogs grow.

chapters.title: Revenue Trajectory, Non-GAAP Burns, and a $569 Million Cash Moat: Rigetti's Financial Architecture
chapters.body:
## The Revenue Record: A Five-Year Contract Ledger

Rigetti Computing's income statement is not a conventional technology revenue story. It is, in the strictest sense, a project-completion ledger — a series of government contract milestones, hardware delivery triggers, and cloud-access subscriptions whose aggregate, over the company's first five fiscal years as a public entity, has never exceeded thirteen million dollars in any single year. Understanding that constraint is essential before any valuation or burn-rate analysis can proceed.

The five-year revenue record, drawn from [10-K and 10-Q filings on SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001838359&type=10-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40), is as follows:

| Fiscal Year | Full-Year Revenue | YoY Change |
|---|---|---|
| FY2021 | ~$8–9M (est., pre-SPAC) | — |
| FY2022 | ~$13M (est.) | — |
| FY2023 | $12.0M | — |
| FY2024 | $10.8M | –10.0% |
| FY2025 | $7.1M | –34.3% |
| Q1 2026 | $4.4M (single quarter) | +193% YoY |

The FY2024 quarterly cadence, drawn from the [FY2024 10-K filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000155837025002499/rgti-20241231x10k.htm), was remarkably flat: Q1 $3.1M, Q2 $3.1M, Q3 $2.4M, Q4 $2.3M — a slow fade across the year that was not a reflection of market-share erosion but of the inherent lumpiness of government R&D contract structures, where milestone payments require deliverable certification before recognition.

The FY2025 decline to $7.1M — the company's lowest full-year revenue since at least FY2022 — followed the same logic. Technology-development agreements with U.S. and UK government agencies moved through their natural lifecycle: mature contracts wound down while new ones entered early performance phases with limited recognition triggers. The revenue decline from FY2023 through FY2025 represents timing-dependent contract accounting, not a deterioration in Rigetti's competitive positioning or customer base. The Q1 2026 inflection to $4.4M on a single quarter — ~~driven by Novera QPU shipment milestones and early recognition on the C-DAC Cepheus order~~ ==driven primarily by higher Novera system and related product sales, including the University of Saskatchewan shipment== — demonstrates precisely how quickly the model can reaccelerate when hardware deliveries begin.

---

## GAAP Versus Non-GAAP: Two Income Statements, One Company

No aspect of Rigetti's financials causes more confusion among first-time readers than the divergence between GAAP and non-GAAP results. The cause is structural and dates to the 2022 SPAC transaction: when Rigetti merged with Supernova Partners Acquisition Company II, it inherited a set of derivative warrant liabilities and earn-out structures whose fair values must be re-marked to market every quarter under GAAP. These are entirely non-cash items that bear no relationship to the company's operating cost structure, but their magnitude can exceed total annual revenue by an order of magnitude in volatile quarters.

The following table illustrates the divergence:

| Period | GAAP Net Loss (Income) | Non-Cash Warrant/Earn-Out Item | Non-GAAP Net Loss | GAAP Operating Loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 2024 | $(153.0M) loss | $(135.1M) charge | ~$(17.9M) | ~$(20M) est. |
| FY2025 | $(216.2M) loss | large non-cash charges | $(50.5M) | — |
| Q4 2025 | — | — | — | $(22.6M) |
| Q1 2026 | $33.1M income | ~~$62.1M~~ ==$53.7M== non-cash gain | $(14.7M) | $(26.0M) |

Sources: [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000110465926023454/rgti-20251231x10k.htm); [Q1 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000110465926058635/rgti-20260511xex99d1.htm).

The Q1 2026 GAAP result — a headline profit of $33.1 million — is particularly instructive. At the operating level, Rigetti burned $26.0 million in the quarter, its largest single-quarter operating loss on record. The swing to GAAP net income came entirely from the ~~$62.1 million~~ ==$53.7 million== non-cash gain recognized when the fair value of its derivative warrant ~~and earn-out~~ liabilities fell, driven by movements in the underlying share price. Analysts who read only the GAAP headline would conclude that Rigetti turned profitable in Q1 2026. Analysts who read the non-GAAP disclosure would correctly conclude it consumed $14.7 million in cash-equivalent losses during the same period.

The operationally relevant metric is non-GAAP net loss, which strips stock-based compensation alongside the warrant and earn-out adjustments. On that basis, the FY2025 loss of $50.5 million implies an average quarterly non-GAAP burn of roughly $12 to $13 million — a number that, set against the company's cash position, produces a very different strategic picture than the $216 million GAAP headline.

---

## Capital Architecture: Building the $569 Million Moat

Rigetti's balance sheet is, paradoxically, one of the strongest in the publicly traded quantum sector. It carries zero long-term debt — an unusual condition for a deep-technology company in a capital-intensive hardware vertical — and as of March 31, 2026, held [$569.0 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000155837025007375/rgti-20250331x10q.htm).

The construction of that position reflects three distinct capital-raising episodes. The SPAC transaction in March 2022 delivered approximately $261.75 million in gross proceeds — the foundational infusion that funded Fab-1 operations, QPU development, and the company's initial post-listing operating budget. By early 2025, however, the cash position had declined substantially as operating losses accumulated. The recovery was driven primarily by the at-the-market equity offering program: during 2025, Rigetti raised $350 million in gross proceeds through ATM sales into what became one of the most dramatic retail-and-institutional quantum sector rallies in the market's history. The third contribution came from Quanta Computer's [$35 million strategic investment at $11.59 per share](https://investors.rigetti.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rigetti-computing-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-yvxoh4p8fn7k), which closed in April 2025 following regulatory clearance.

The year-end 2025 cash balance of $589.8 million modestly declined to $569.0 million by March 31, 2026 — implying approximately $20.8 million in net cash consumption during Q1 2026. Against the non-GAAP operating loss of $14.7 million for the same quarter, the gap reflects working capital movements, capital expenditures, and the modest cash inflow from Q1 revenues of $4.4 million. Annualizing the $20.8 million quarterly net cash draw yields approximately $83 million per year; at that pace, the current $569 million cash position would sustain operations for approximately six to seven years without raising additional capital.

The more conservative planning assumption — using the non-GAAP net loss rate of $14.7 million per quarter and assuming revenue growth partially offsets operating costs — implies a runway extending well past 2033. For context: that is longer than the time horizon that most industry projections cite for fault-tolerant quantum advantage to become commercially relevant.

---

## The Dilution Cost: 107 Million New Shares in Twelve Months

The cash moat has not come without a per-share cost. Between early 2025 and March 31, 2026, Rigetti's ~~diluted share count~~ ==shares outstanding== grew from approximately 225 million to [~~332.4 million~~ ==332.3 million==](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000110465926058635/rgti-20260511xex99d1.htm) — an increase of roughly 107 million shares, or 47.6 percent, in under twelve months.

The ATM program accounts for the majority of that increase. Across the $350 million raised during 2025 and Quanta's $35 million at $11.59 per share (approximately 3.02 million shares), total new issuance was approximately $385 million for roughly 104 to 107 million new shares — implying a blended average issuance price in the range of $3.50 to $3.70 per share. That figure reflects the timing distribution of the ATM sales, heavily weighted toward the earlier months of 2025 when the stock traded at considerably lower levels before the sector rally drove RGTI from approximately $1.96 per share in January to a December implied price that supported the $7.32 billion market capitalization.

The consequence for existing shareholders is significant. An investor who held one percent of Rigetti in early 2025 — 2.25 million shares — held approximately 0.68 percent of the company by Q1 2026, after 107 million new shares entered the float. On a per-share basis, the dilution was partially offset by the extraordinary share-price appreciation the ATM program itself helped fund: the company's enterprise value grew from approximately $441.6 million in January 2025 to $7.32 billion by December 2025, a 1,555 percent gain, suggesting that the capital infusion was perceived by the market as value-creating rather than value-destructive.

Whether continued ATM activity at current levels would be similarly received is a more open question. With ~~332.4 million~~ ==332.3 million== shares outstanding and a current share price implied by the $8.79 billion market capitalization at approximately $26.45, every 10 million new shares issued under a future ATM would raise approximately $264 million in proceeds while diluting existing holders by an additional 2.9 percent. The arithmetic suggests diminishing absolute dilution relative to cash raised, but the political economy of serial equity issuance in a retail-heavy shareholder base requires management to demonstrate clear milestones justifying each incremental capital raise.

---

## Valuation Architecture: Option Theory, Not Discounted Cash Flow

At $8.79 billion market capitalization against $7.1 million in trailing twelve-month revenue, Rigetti trades at a multiple — exceeding 400 times on a trailing revenue basis — that renders conventional earnings-based or discounted-cash-flow frameworks analytically incoherent. No plausible five-year revenue projection, even under the most aggressive quantum-adoption scenario, would generate a net present value approaching the current enterprise value using a conventional cost of capital.

The appropriate framework is not DCF but option pricing. Rigetti is a long-duration call option on the superconducting qubit roadmap: the underlying asset is the total addressable revenue of the quantum computing market if practical advantage materializes between 2028 and 2032; the strike price is the additional capital and execution required to get there; the time value is the company's multi-year runway. On that framework, the $8.79 billion valuation embeds a market estimate of the probability-weighted value of capturing a meaningful share of a market that McKinsey, BCG, and various government science agencies have variously projected at $450 billion to $850 billion annually by the mid-2030s.

A peer comparison is instructive, if limited. [IonQ](https://ionq.com/), the leading publicly traded trapped-ion quantum company, reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $130 million — roughly 18 times Rigetti's — yet its market capitalization of approximately $8 billion sits in a comparable range. The implied revenue multiple on IonQ is approximately 62 times — still speculative by any classical-technology standard, but meaningfully more grounded than Rigetti's. D-Wave Quantum trades at a smaller capitalization on minimal hardware revenue. The divergence suggests that the market is not primarily pricing current revenue but rather assigning probability mass to different technology vectors: trapped-ion, superconducting, and photonic are all optioned by different investor cohorts simultaneously, with the superconducting path — favored by IBM and Google alongside Rigetti — commanding a premium on volume-production plausibility.

---

## Forward Revenue Architecture: From Contracts to Conversion

The financial architecture's next chapter is defined by four specific near-term revenue vectors. The [C-DAC $8.4 million contract](https://investors.rigetti.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rigetti-computing-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-yvxoh4p8fn7k) for a 108-qubit Cepheus-class on-premises system, to be delivered in the second half of 2026, represents Rigetti's largest single hardware order to date; assuming delivery occurs on schedule, the majority of the remaining contract value should recognize in the third and fourth quarters of 2026. The Novera QPU backlog — encompassing the Japanese research institution order, the ~~Air Force Research Laboratory deployments~~ ==SQMS/Fermilab installation, the Air Force Research Laboratory deployment==, and the UK NQCC relationship — provides a continuing stream of sub-$1 million hardware transactions that, in aggregate, establish recurring post-delivery service relationships.

The Department of Commerce letter of intent for up to $100 million in quantum R&D funding, ~~signed in March 2026~~ ==announced May 21, 2026==, represents the largest potential near-term government capital inflow. ==Because the LOI contemplates an equity stake for the Department, a conversion to formal funding would not be cleanly non-dilutive.== The LOI is not yet a contract, and the conversion timeline is not publicly established, but a partial drawdown in the $20 to $40 million range — consistent with how similar DOC programs have structured initial tranches — would materially alter Rigetti's FY2026 revenue profile.

The Quanta Computer commercial pipeline remains the most difficult to quantify but potentially the most transformative. Quanta's stated commitment to invest more than $100 million alongside Rigetti over five years, combined with its engineering and distribution relationships with hyperscale data center operators, creates a channel through which Cepheus-class and next-generation systems could enter enterprise procurement cycles at a scale Rigetti could not access through direct government-only sales.

Management guided during the [Q4 2025 earnings call](https://investors.rigetti.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rigetti-computing-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024) to "significant first-quarter year-over-year revenue growth" for 2026 — a guidance range that Q1's $4.4 million result confirmed and exceeded. The company has not issued full-year 2026 revenue guidance, consistent with the milestone-dependent nature of contract recognition. What the financial architecture has provided, through its $569 million cash moat and zero-debt balance sheet, is the operational latitude to pursue those milestones without capital constraint — a condition that, as of the frozen snapshot date, no superconducting quantum pure-play in the public market can match.

chapters.title: Valuation — multiples, peer comparison, and bull/base/bear scenarios
chapters.body:
## The Multiple That Defies Fundamental Logic

At the frozen snapshot of May 23, 2026, Rigetti Computing carried a market capitalisation of approximately $8.79 billion and an enterprise value — netting out $569.0 million in cash and investments held as of March 31, 2026, against zero long-term debt — of roughly $8.22 billion. Against trailing twelve-month revenue of approximately $10 million (reconstructed from FY2025's $7.1 million after adjusting for the year-over-year composition shift), the implied EV/Sales multiple approaches 820 times. Annualised on Rigetti's Q1 2026 result of $4.4 million — the first quarter embedding material hardware-contract revenue — the multiple compresses toward 467 times. Either figure places Rigetti at the outer boundary of the speculative-technology pricing spectrum.

These multiples cannot be rationalised through conventional discounted cash flow. They represent option pricing: the market's probability-weighted assessment of the enterprise value Rigetti would command if superconducting quantum computing achieves commercial-scale practical advantage. Valuation analysis must therefore disaggregate three distinct layers — the applicable metrics and their structural limits, the peer-relative calibration, and the scenario tree that maps technical milestones to price outcomes.

## Applicable Multiples and Their Limits

Standard earnings-based multiples are inapplicable. GAAP net loss for FY2025 was $216.2 million, artificially amplified by non-cash derivative warrant and earn-out liabilities inherited from the 2022 SPAC transaction; the operationally meaningful [non-GAAP net loss was $50.5 million](https://investors.rigetti.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rigetti-computing-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-yvxoh4p8fn7k). Both render P/E irrelevant. EV/EBITDA is similarly inapplicable. The operative multiples are EV/Sales and price-to-cash.

Price-to-cash offers a floor reading. With approximately ~~332.4 million diluted shares~~ ==332.3 million shares outstanding== implying a share price of roughly $26.45 and $569.0 million in cash, the per-share cash value is approximately $1.71 — producing a price-to-cash ratio of approximately 15.5 times. That ratio quantifies the pure option premium the market is assigning to QPU intellectual property, fabrication infrastructure, and the commercialisation roadmap beyond hard net assets.

On a forward basis, using conservative consensus expectations that FY2026 revenue could reach $20–30 million as C-DAC Cepheus-class delivery milestones and Novera backlog fulfilment recognise revenue, the forward EV/Sales multiple compresses to approximately 275–410 times — still extraordinary by classical-technology standards, but directionally consistent with a revenue inflection.

## Historical Multiple Range: From Deep De-Rating to Speculative Peak

Rigetti's own multiple history is short and violent. The company listed in March 2022 at an initial market capitalisation of approximately $1.5 billion; eighteen months of post-SPAC hangover and rising interest rates compressed it to roughly $441.6 million by January 2025 — a 70 percent de-rating from listing. The reversal was equally extreme: [the market capitalisation rose from $441.6 million in January 2025 to $7.32 billion by December 2025](https://investors.rigetti.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rigetti-computing-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-yvxoh4p8fn7k), a 1,555 percent appreciation driven by the Quanta Computer strategic partnership, ~~the Department of Commerce letter of intent,~~ the Ankaa-3 99.0 percent median iSWAP gate-fidelity benchmark, and a broad quantum sector re-rating that lifted all listed peers. The stock subsequently recovered to approximately $8.79 billion by May 22, 2026.

The implication is structural: Rigetti's multiple has no anchor in operating fundamentals. A company that traded at approximately 40 times trailing revenue in early 2025 and now trades at 820 times on the same revenue base has re-rated entirely on narrative upgrade rather than earnings improvement. That bi-directionality defines the dominant risk in both directions.

## Peer-Group Multiple Comparison

The listed comparable universe is thin. IBM and Google operate superconducting quantum divisions within businesses generating tens of billions in consolidated revenue, making quantum-specific multiples unobservable. Quantinuum (Honeywell-backed) and PsiQuantum remain private. The meaningful listed peers are:

| Company | Ticker | Approx. Mkt Cap | FY2025 Rev | Approx. EV/Sales | Modality |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rigetti Computing | RGTI | $8.79B | $7.1M | ~820x (TTM) | Superconducting |
| IonQ | IONQ | ~$8.0B | $130M | ~60x | Trapped-ion |
| D-Wave Quantum | QBTS | ~$2.0B | ~$12M | ~160x | Quantum annealing |
| Quantum Computing Inc. | QUBT | ~$0.8B | ~$2M | ~400x | Photonic/CMOS |

*Peer market caps and revenue are approximate public-market estimates as of the frozen snapshot; D-Wave and QUBT figures estimated from publicly available filings.*

IonQ's profile is the most instructive comparator. At $130 million in FY2025 revenue — eighteen times Rigetti's trailing base — IonQ trades at approximately 60 times EV/Sales, a multiple that reflects genuinely scaled commercial revenue beginning to provide fundamental support. Rigetti's premium over IonQ on an EV/Sales basis of roughly 14-to-1 is not supported by a corresponding technical or market-position differential; it reflects a smaller float, higher beta, and the momentum-amplifying dynamics of retail and algorithmic participation in pure-play quantum names. The peer table's central message is that Rigetti is not merely priced at a quantum premium — it is priced at a quantum premium relative to other quantum premiums.

## Intrinsic Value: The Cash-Flow Trajectory the Price Implies

Working backward from an $8.22 billion enterprise value at a 15 percent discount rate appropriate to a pre-commercial deep-technology company, the current price embeds one of two implicit assumptions: either Rigetti reaches approximately $1.5–2.0 billion in annual revenue by the mid-2030s with operating margins converging toward 30 percent, or the terminal value is being assigned on a speculative multiple that will need to compress materially before the business reaches cash-flow breakeven.

The $1.5–2.0 billion revenue target requires quantum computing to achieve fault-tolerant utility — conventionally modelled at 1,000-plus logical qubits — and Rigetti to capture a meaningful share of the resulting enterprise and government hardware market. Rigetti's ~~March 2026 announcement of a greater-than-1,000-qubit UK deployment investment, its DOC letter of intent for up to $100 million in R&D funding~~ ==March 2026 announcement of a planned up to US$100 million UK investment anchored on a greater-than-1,000-qubit deployment, the May 2026 DOC letter of intent contemplating R&D funding alongside an equity stake for the Department==, and the Quanta Computer distribution partnership map a credible path to that revenue scale. But "credible path" in a technology with no validated commercial use case at scale is not equivalent to "probable outcome." The DCF exercise confirms the current price is not incoherent given the size of the prize; it requires near-perfect execution across technical, commercial, and geopolitical dimensions simultaneously.

## Bull, Base, and Bear Scenarios

**Bull scenario — $40–50 per share:** The ~~DOC funding converts fully~~ ==DOC LOI converts into a formal award on terms that include the contemplated equity stake==; the UK 1,000-qubit deployment completes ahead of schedule in 2028; C-DAC triggers follow-on contracts across South and Southeast Asia; and the Quanta Computer global distribution channel unlocks the first hyperscale data-centre QPU purchase order. Revenue reaches $150 million in FY2028 and $350 million by FY2030, combining hardware sales, recurring service contracts, and cloud-access subscriptions. At 30 times EV/Sales on FY2030 revenue, enterprise value reaches approximately $10.5 billion; adding residual cash of approximately $400 million implies a market cap of $10.9 billion and a share price of $40–50, assuming modest additional dilution. Multiple expansion beyond 30 times — plausible if Rigetti is the first company to demonstrate commercially validated quantum advantage — could push the bull case above $60.

**Base scenario — $20–28 per share:** Hardware contracts execute on schedule without acceleration; cloud revenue grows modestly; no transformational enterprise contract materialises before 2028; the quantum sector sustains its narrative premium through continued government-spending tailwinds. Revenue reaches $50 million by FY2027 and $100 million by FY2029. On these assumptions, the current $8.22 billion EV implies approximately 164 times FY2027 EV/Sales — still generous but directionally compressing. The base case is effectively price stability through 2026–2027 as revenue growth absorbs the excess multiple: market cap of $8–9 billion, share price of $24–28.

**Bear scenario — $4–8 per share:** A quantum sector de-rating mirrors the 2022–2024 drawdown — whether driven by rising discount rates, a high-profile IBM or Google demonstration that structurally repositions Rigetti as subscale, or technical delays in the 1,000-qubit roadmap. Revenue stagnates below $20 million through 2028; the EV/Sales multiple compresses toward 50 times (still generous for a stagnating business), implying enterprise value of approximately $1.0 billion and a market cap of $1.6 billion. That produces a share price of roughly $4–5 per ~~diluted~~ share — approximately double the per-share cash value of $1.71, reflecting residual option value in the fabrication assets and intellectual property but almost no commercial-trajectory premium.

## The Consensus Gap

The market at $8.79 billion is pricing somewhere between the bull and optimistic-base cases: continued technical momentum, partial hardware pipeline conversion, and sustained narrative premium. What it is not pricing is execution risk. A disciplined EV/Sales compression to 100 times on even $30 million in FY2026 revenue produces an EV of $3.0 billion — a more than 60 percent discount to today's enterprise value.

The dossier's read is that the current valuation is defensible as a real-option price rather than a fundamental equity price. Rigetti's $569 million cash position provides ~~four-plus years~~ ==approximately a decade== of operational insulation at current burn rates. The Quanta partnership inserts a credible commercialisation pathway that no prior Rigetti management team possessed. The technical roadmap from 108-qubit Cepheus to a 1,000-qubit UK deployment represents the most concrete multi-year hardware commitment in the company's history. But investors accepting today's price are implicitly accepting that practical quantum advantage is a question of timing, not existence — and that Rigetti will be among the surviving pure-plays when it arrives. Those two embedded assumptions carry substantially more analytical weight than any discounted-cash-flow model was designed to absorb.

chapters.title: Quarterly Cadence and Management Commentary: From Post-SPAC Turbulence to the 2026 Inflection
chapters.body:
## The Post-SPAC Baseline: A Revenue Sequence Under Pressure

When Rigetti Computing completed its SPAC merger in March 2022 and began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker RGTI, the company inherited an unusual financial profile: modest but real government-contract revenue, a freshly public balance sheet, and a cost structure calibrated for a private company still searching for product-market fit. The quarters that followed were defined by the structural awkwardness of that transition. Revenue in FY2023 reached $12.0 million, declining to $10.8 million in FY2024 as milestone timing on government technology-development contracts created uneven quarterly flows. That revenue base — almost entirely constituted by U.S. and UK government research agreements and supplementary cloud access subscriptions — offered analysts little of the recurring-revenue predictability they were accustomed to pricing.

The quarterly cadence across 2024 reflected that volatility. The year's best single revenue quarter was not the final one: Q4 2024, released by Rigetti on March 5, 2025, came in at $2.3 million — a sequential step down that underscored the lumpiness inherent in contract-based government revenue. GAAP operating loss for the quarter was $18.5 million, itself overshadowed by a GAAP net loss of $153.0 million. The headline required immediate disaggregation: embedded within it was approximately $135.1 million in non-cash charges arising from fair-value remeasurements of derivative warrant and earn-out liabilities inherited from the Supernova SPAC structure. Stripped of those items, the operational picture was far less dramatic — though still indicative of a company burning through equity capital to reach commercialization milestones that remained, in early 2025, largely prospective.

## The Quanta Catalyst: Q4 2024 Earnings in Context (March 5, 2025)

The Q4 2024 release landed in the same week as a corporate announcement of considerably greater strategic weight. On February 27, 2025, Rigetti disclosed a [strategic collaboration agreement with Quanta Computer Inc.](https://investors.rigetti.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rigetti-computing-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024) — the Taiwanese contract manufacturing giant whose approximately $43 billion in annual revenue spans global data-center supply chains and hyperscale server production. Under the terms of the partnership, both parties committed to investing more than $100 million each over five years to develop superconducting quantum computing products; Quanta separately agreed to take a $35 million equity stake at $11.59 per share, a transaction that closed in April 2025 following regulatory clearance. Management presented the relationship as a structural inflection point: where prior partnerships had been research-oriented or regionally specific, Quanta offered manufacturing scale, global distribution infrastructure, and direct channels to the enterprise and government customers that Rigetti's direct sales force could not efficiently reach. The juxtaposition — a $153 million GAAP loss report alongside a transformational manufacturing partnership — compressed what would otherwise have been distinct financial and strategic news cycles into a single investor communication event.

## The Cycle Trough: Q1 2025 (May 12, 2025)

The quarter ending March 31, 2025 produced Rigetti's weakest revenue of the reported cycle. At $1.5 million, Q1 2025 marked the nadir of a revenue sequence that had been declining since FY2023 — the combined effect of contract milestone timing, the absence of large new hardware orders, and the transitional period between Ankaa-class and Cepheus-class system deployments. GAAP operating loss widened to $21.6 million, reflecting the build-out of engineering and fabrication capacity ahead of the next product generation. The GAAP headline, however, was again inverted by non-cash derivative movements: a $62.1 million non-cash gain from warrant and earn-out revaluations produced a reported GAAP net income of $42.6 million — a number that accurately described nothing about the company's operational state.

Management used the Q1 2025 release to redirect attention toward two operational developments. First, [Ankaa-3](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000155837025007375/rgti-20250331x10q.htm) — the 84-qubit successor launched in December 2024 with a then-record 99.0% median iSWAP gate fidelity and 99.5% median fidelity using fSim gates — had reached full deployment on QCS and was accessible through AWS Braket and Microsoft Azure. Second, the Novera QPU Partner Program, formally launched in April 2024, had accumulated additional deployments beyond the ~~initial Air Force Research Laboratory units~~ ==initial deployments to Fermilab's Superconducting Quantum Materials and Systems Center and the Air Force Research Laboratory==: systems had reached the Israeli Quantum Computing Center, co-located with NVIDIA Grace-Hopper servers, and new institutional partners. The message was deliberate — the revenue trough was a timing artifact, not a demand signal, and the on-premises hardware pipeline was converting.

## Mid-Year Reconstruction: Q2 and Q3 2025

With Q1 2025 revenue at $1.5 million and the full-year FY2025 figure ultimately settling at $7.1 million, the arithmetic implied that Q2 and Q3 2025 collectively contributed approximately $3.7 million — a modest but sequential improvement off the trough. The Q3 2025 earnings release carried a specific disclosure of strategic weight: Rigetti published what it characterized as "Technology Roadmap Updates for 2026 and 2027," offering the market its clearest forward architecture statement yet. The roadmap detailed the progression from the Cepheus-1-108Q chiplet-based architecture then in late-stage development toward a greater-than-1,000-qubit system targeted for UK deployment, underpinned by continued fidelity improvements. Separately, the disclosure that a prototype system had achieved 99.9% two-qubit gate fidelity at 28-nanosecond gate speed served as the technical punctuation mark for the year's second half — evidence that the company's internal R&D trajectory was tracking against the claims made to investors and government partners.

Through mid-2025, the consistent messaging cadence from both Kulkarni and CFO Jeffrey Bertelsen anchored each quarterly release to fidelity milestones as sequential proof points. Each hardware generation — Ankaa-2, Ankaa-3, and the forthcoming Cepheus architecture — was framed not primarily as a revenue event but as evidence that superconducting gate fidelity was converging on the thresholds required for practical quantum advantage.

## Q4 2025 and the Full-Year Reckoning (March 4, 2026)

Rigetti released Q4 and full-year 2025 results on March 4, 2026. The headline figures were soft by the structure of the contract model: Q4 2025 revenue came in at $1.9 million — seasonally compressed — while the full-year total reached $7.1 million, below both FY2024's $10.8 million and FY2023's $12.0 million. The [GAAP operating loss](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000110465926023446/rgti-20260304xex99d1.htm) for Q4 2025 was $22.6 million; the non-GAAP net loss for the full year was $50.5 million, implying a quarterly cash-operational burn in the range of $12–15 million. The balance sheet, however, had been materially transformed: cash, cash equivalents, and investments stood at $589.8 million at year-end 2025 — the product of $350 million raised through the at-the-market equity offering during 2025 and the $35 million Quanta injection — against zero long-term debt.

> "Great progress across fidelity, scale, and system architecture."

Kulkarni's framing for Q4 2025 reprised the language that had characterized every prior period's prepared remarks. The phrase was not accidental: it anchored the company's narrative to technical execution — fidelity, qubit count, modular architecture — rather than near-term revenue metrics, a framing consistent with both the pre-commercial reality and the investor base's revealed preference for hardware milestones over incremental contract wins.

## Q1 2026: The Inflection (May 11, 2026)

The quarter ending March 31, 2026 produced the data point Rigetti's management had been forecasting for two years. [Revenue of $4.4 million](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000110465926058635/rgti-20260511xex99d1.htm) represented a 193 percent increase year-over-year — the company's fastest growth rate since going public — driven ~~by partial recognition of Novera QPU shipment milestones, Cepheus-class system orders, and the accrual of the approximately $8.4 million C-DAC contract for a 108-qubit on-premises deployment in India~~ ==primarily by higher Novera system and related product sales, including a Novera QPU shipment to the University of Saskatchewan==. The Cepheus-1-108Q ~~had achieved general availability during the quarter~~ ==would be announced as generally available on April 7, 2026, shortly after the quarter closed==, with subsequent cloud access and on-premises orders anchoring the hardware pipeline.

The GAAP and non-GAAP figures once again diverged sharply: GAAP net income of $33.1 million was produced entirely by non-cash derivative revaluations, while the non-GAAP net loss was $14.7 million and the GAAP operating loss was $26.0 million. Cash stood at $569.0 million — a modest drawdown from year-end — with no debt. The broader strategic context amplified the earnings signal: ~~in March 2026,~~ Rigetti had signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce ==on May 21, 2026== for up to $100 million in R&D funding under national quantum computing programs ==that contemplated an equity stake for the Department==, and ~~simultaneously~~ ==separately== committed up to $100 million in UK investment over three to four years for a greater-than-1,000-qubit system at the National Quantum Computing Centre in Didcot. RGTI shares gained 8.24 percent during regular trading on May 11 before declining 1.85 percent in the after-hours session — a pattern consistent with investors processing the gap between the GAAP income headline and the underlying non-GAAP operating loss.

The management commentary across every period from Q4 2024 through Q1 2026 was notable precisely for its consistency: fidelity milestones, not revenue metrics, were offered as the primary evidence of strategic progress, a rhetorical posture that either reflected disciplined alignment between internal execution and external communication, or deferred the commercial accounting to a later date that management, as of May 2026, believed had finally arrived.

chapters.title: The CyberOptics Alumni at the Helm: CEO Kulkarni, CFO Bertelsen, and the Post-Founder Governance Reset
chapters.body:
## The Commercial Operator Thesis

When Rigetti Computing's board began searching for a new chief executive in the autumn of 2022, it did not dispatch a recruiter to the quantum physics departments of MIT, Caltech, or Stanford. It looked instead toward the semiconductor supply chain — specifically to a precision sensors company headquartered in Minneapolis called CyberOptics Corporation, where a chemical engineer named Subodh Kulkarni had spent eight years turning advanced optical measurement technology into a profitable and ultimately acquired business.

The choice, announced in [December 2022](https://investors.rigetti.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rigetti-computing-appoints-dr-subodh-kulkarni-president-and), was a declaration of intent. Rigetti had listed on Nasdaq in March 2022 through a SPAC merger with Supernova Partners Acquisition Company II, raised approximately $261.75 million in gross proceeds, and ~~then watched its founder-CEO Chad Rigetti depart within weeks of the first day of trading~~ ==then announced later in 2022 that founder-CEO Chad Rigetti would step down, with the search for a successor beginning that autumn==. The board's answer to the question of what came next was not a deeper immersion in quantum mechanics but a sharper focus on commercialization discipline: find a seasoned hardware executive who understood how to build a sales pipeline, manage an engineering-to-delivery cycle, and eventually satisfy the revenue expectations of public-market investors.

Dr. Kulkarni arrived carrying credentials assembled across three decades of high-performance materials and computing. He earned a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai, before completing a master's and doctorate in chemical engineering at MIT — a scientific foundation that gave him fluency in the physics of thin-film deposition and semiconductor process chemistry, even if his career trajectory bent toward management rather than laboratory research. After MIT he joined 3M, where he worked on advanced materials development, then moved to IBM's research division before ultimately joining Imation Corporation — a data storage and imaging spinout of 3M — where he rose to Chief Technology Officer and Senior Vice President of OEM and Emerging Business, overseeing product portfolios that competed in precision optics and digital media.

By the time he became CEO of Prism Computational Sciences, a developer of scientific software for the semiconductor industry, Kulkarni had accumulated the exact resume combination the post-SPAC Rigetti board believed the company needed: scientific credibility, technology commercialization experience, and a demonstrated ability to lead a business from development-stage operations to an acquirable exit. That combination was on full display at CyberOptics, where he served as President and CEO from 2014 until November 2022. Under his leadership, CyberOptics scaled its precision sensor and inspection systems business — products used in semiconductor wafer handling and electronics manufacturing — and completed a successful acquisition by Nordson Corporation at a premium to prior trading levels. The Nordson deal closed, Kulkarni left, and within months he had accepted the Rigetti appointment.

## The CyberOptics Alumni Network

Less than three months after Kulkarni joined, Rigetti announced that Jeffrey Bertelsen would become its Chief Financial Officer, [effective February 2023](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000119312523031410/d406416dex991.htm). The two men had worked together continuously at CyberOptics from 2005 to 2022 — Bertelsen as CFO and later COO, Kulkarni as CEO — developing the kind of institutional shorthand and mutual operational trust that external executive searches rarely produce. In a company navigating the pressures of post-SPAC governance reform, escalating R&D costs, and the need to articulate a credible commercialization roadmap to skeptical institutional investors, that pre-formed working relationship was a material asset.

Bertelsen brought more than twenty-five years of high-technology finance experience to Rigetti. His disclosed total compensation for fiscal year 2025 was $1,908,499, inclusive of base salary, cash incentives, and restricted stock unit awards — a figure consistent with CFO market rates at a mid-cap technology company and modest relative to the equity upside available if Rigetti's quantum hardware programs converted into recurring revenue. The more telling data point arrived in May 2026, when Bertelsen filed a Form 4 disclosing the sale of 3,682 shares at $22.95 per share — a transaction that generated approximately $84,500 in proceeds. In isolation the figure was negligible relative to his overall compensation. In context it was notable: RGTI shares had appreciated approximately 1,555% during 2025, rising from a low single-digit price to a range that implied an enterprise value of approximately $8.8 billion. A CFO selling a small tranche of shares after such a run is routine portfolio management, not a governance alarm — but the transaction illustrated the scale of value that had accreted to insiders through equity compensation during a period when the company's revenue remained below $10 million annually.

## The Technical Counterweight

The appointment of David Rivas as Chief Technology Officer, also in [February 2023](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838359/000110465926023454/rgti-20251231x10k.htm), completed the executive team's construction. Rivas arrived to serve as the direct interface between Rigetti's scientific and engineering capabilities and the operational leadership team — providing the technical pedigree that neither Kulkarni nor Bertelsen possessed in quantum systems specifically. As CTO, his mandate encompassed oversight of the Fab-1 engineering team in Fremont, where Rigetti fabricates superconducting QPUs in-house using process chemistry derived from conventional semiconductor manufacturing, and strategic responsibility for the roadmap progression from the 84-qubit Ankaa family through the 108-qubit Cepheus-1 chiplet architecture toward the greater-than-1,000-qubit systems described in the company's public roadmap commitments. The structure assigned Rivas accountability for the gate fidelity milestones — including the ~~99.5% median fSim fidelity achieved on Cepheus-1 at general availability~~ ==99.1% current median two-qubit gate fidelity disclosed at Cepheus-1's April 7, 2026 general availability, with 99.5% set as a later-2026 target,== and the 99.9% two-qubit gate fidelity demonstrated on a 2025 prototype — that underpin every commercial claim Kulkarni makes on earnings calls.

## The Board's Deliberate Composition

The governance layer above the executive team reflected the same commercial-over-scientific logic. Thomas J. Iannotti, named Independent Board Chair effective October 31, 2023, came to Rigetti from HP Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise, where he had spent decades in enterprise technology sales, services, and general management. His appointment as chair — succeeding Cathy McCarthy, who remained on the board as a continuing director — signaled the post-SPAC normalization of Rigetti's governance structure toward conventional independent-chair practices. The board's committee structure, as disclosed in the 2026 DEF 14A proxy statement, assigns Audit Committee responsibility to directors with enterprise finance and technology backgrounds — critical given that Rigetti's GAAP results are periodically distorted by non-cash fair-value swings on SPAC-era derivative warrant and earn-out liabilities that have exceeded $100 million in a single period.

Notably absent from the boardroom, as of the 2026 proxy, was any director with a formal background in quantum physics or quantum computing research. The composition — enterprise IT, semiconductor supply chain, financial services — represented a conscious choice to prioritize commercial governance over technical oversight from the board level, leaving scientific judgment to the CTO and the engineering organization.
