Of these, molecular simulation aligns most directly with Rigetti's architecture: superconducting transmon qubits, operating at nanosecond gate speeds, are better suited to the variational quantum eigensolver and quantum phase estimation algorithms used in chemistry simulation than to the deep circuits required for Grover-style database search or Shor's factoring.

Rigetti's existing relationships with national laboratories and defense contractors position it to capture the first wave of government-funded quantum advantage demonstrations. The more uncertain question is whether those demonstrations will convert into commercially licensable advantage — meaning a quantum result that a paying enterprise could not obtain with classical hardware at an acceptable cost. The 2028-2030 window is when most independent technical assessments expect 1,000-plus-qubit systems with error correction to first become available; whether Rigetti, IBM, IonQ, or Quantinuum produces the first commercially validated result will determine which company captures the reference contract that anchors enterprise pricing expectations for the decade.

Rigetti's positioning in this window is defensible but not dominant. Its fidelity trajectory is the strongest per-qubit performance narrative among pure-play public companies. But IonQ reported $130 million in FY2025 revenue against Rigetti's $7.1 million, commanding enterprise relationships that Rigetti has not yet established. IBM's superconducting program is not ring-fenced for competitive comparison but represents engineering resources at a scale Rigetti cannot match. Quantinuum's trapped-ion systems have claimed 99.99 percent gate accuracy and are actively pursuing pharmaceutical and financial enterprise contracts. Rigetti's path to capturing first-mover advantage contracts requires that gate speed — superconducting's structural advantage over trapped-ion — becomes the binding constraint in the first practical applications, rather than gate fidelity per shot or circuit depth, where trapped-ion currently leads.

## Capital Structure Through 2030: Funding Adequacy and Dilution Risk

The $569 million cash position as of March 31, 2026, against a non-GAAP operating cash burn of approximately $12 million to $15 million per quarter, implies a runway extending ~~to roughly 2028 or 2029~~ ==well into the mid-2030s== at current spending levels. However, the UK facility investment — up to $100 million over three to four years — and the Quanta collaboration programs will require accelerated capital deployment. ~~The DOC and UK government funding commitments, if they convert from LOI to formal grants, could substitute for equity raises totaling $150 million to $200 million through 2028, materially improving the dilution trajectory.~~ ==The DOC LOI, if it converts into a formal grant award, could offset some near-term equity needs through 2028, but it would not be cleanly non-dilutive because the LOI contemplated an equity stake for the Department; the UK announcement, by contrast, is Rigetti's own planned outbound investment in the United Kingdom rather than funding flowing into Rigetti, and so does not on its own improve the dilution trajectory.==

The base case, absent that substitution, is that shares outstanding — already ~~332.4~~ ==332.3== million after 47.6 percent year-over-year growth — approach 400 million to 450 million by 2029 as the company funds fabrication capacity expansion through further at-the-market offerings. Each 10 percent increase in share count at current prices represents approximately $880 million in theoretical dilution headroom, which is sufficient to fund operations, but at the cost of progressive per-share value compression.

## Bull and Bear: Two Futures by 2030

The bull scenario rests on a cascade: fidelity milestones at 500-plus qubits, demonstrated on the UK system by 2028, convert to enterprise proof-of-concept contracts with hyperscale operators via Quanta's distribution channel; the DOC grant award funds a domestic 1,000-qubit fabrication push; one or two pharmaceutical or financial optimization customers sign multi-year software access agreements that establish subscription revenue. On this path, FY2028 revenue crosses $50 million, the company approaches non-GAAP operating breakeven, and the speculative premium in the stock price becomes, for the first time, anchored in visible forward earnings.

The bear scenario is more probable in the near term. Government contracts continue to represent more than 80 percent of revenue; enterprise customers wait for demonstrated advantage on their specific workloads before committing procurement budgets; IBM or IonQ captures the first publicized quantum advantage result in drug discovery or portfolio optimization, locking in reference relationships; and the UK and DOC commitments slip by eighteen to twenty-four months due to procurement bureaucracy. In that scenario, Rigetti burns through its cash reserves and is forced into a highly dilutive equity raise — or a strategic transaction — before commercial break-even is achieved.

The $569 million cash war chest buys time, but it does not buy certainty. The 2026-2027 period is when the distance between those two futures begins to narrow.

financials.key_finding: Rigetti Computing's financial profile is that of a pre-commercial deep-technology company operating on the speculative frontier of quantum hardware. Full-year 2025 revenue was $7.1 million — a decline from $10.8 million in FY2024 and $12.0 million in FY2023 — driven by the timing-dependent nature of government technology-development contract milestones and the slow ramp of on-premises QPU orders. The revenue composition is almost entirely contract-based: technology development agreements with government agencies, national laboratories, and research institutions, supplemented by modest cloud-access subscriptions via QCS, Amazon Web Services Braket, and Microsoft Azure. GAAP net loss for FY2025 was $216.2 million, an artificially elevated figure that includes large non-cash charges from changes in the fair value of derivative warrant and earn-out liabilities — a structural artifact of the 2022 SPAC transaction. The more operationally meaningful non-GAAP net loss was $50.5 million for FY2025, reflecting actual cash-based research, development, and general and administrative spending. The company's capital structure is notable for two reasons: first, an absence of debt as of March 31, 2026, and second, a cash, cash equivalents, and investments balance of $569.0 million — the product of a $350 million at-the-market equity offering completed during 2025 plus Quanta Computer's $35 million strategic investment in April 2025 at $11.59 per share. The Q1 2026 results signal the first meaningful inflection: revenue of $4.4 million grew 193 percent year-over-year, driven by partial recognition of Novera QPU shipment milestones and Cepheus-class system orders including the C-DAC ($8.4 million) contract. The company carries approximately 332.4 million diluted shares outstanding and traded at a market capitalization of approximately $8.79 billion as of May 22, 2026 — implying a revenue multiple exceeding 400x on a trailing twelve-month basis, which is consistent with speculative quantum sector pricing rather than fundamental earnings power. Forward variables are dominated by the pace of hardware contract conversion: the C-DAC 108-qubit delivery (expected H2 2026), Novera QPU backlog fulfillment, and any enterprise or hyperscale cloud contracts enabled by the Quanta Computer partnership.
structural_observations: Revenue base is small and contract-dependent: FY2023 $12.0M → FY2024 $10.8M → FY2025 $7.1M → Q1 2026 $4.4M (193% YoY), with all periods dominated by U.S. and UK government technology-development contracts rather than commercial enterprise sales; no meaningful subscription revenue has been disclosed.

Fiscal year cadence is December 31; quarterly earnings are reported roughly 60-70 days after quarter-end — Q4/full-year 2025 results were released March 4, 2026; Q1 2026 results were released May 11, 2026 — creating a meaningful information lag relative to the company's fast-moving technical milestones.

Margin structure is pre-commercialization: GAAP operating losses ran $22.6M in Q4 2025 and $26.0M in Q1 2026; non-GAAP operating losses (excluding stock-based compensation and non-cash warrant/earn-out fair-value adjustments) are more stable but still substantial relative to revenue, with the non-GAAP net loss of $50.5M for FY2025 implying an operating cash burn of roughly $12-15M per quarter; gross margins are not meaningfully reported due to the contract-revenue model.

Capital structure is equity-only with no debt: $569.0M in cash and investments as of March 31, 2026, versus zero long-term debt; the balance sheet is a function of successive ATM equity offerings (including $350M raised during 2025) and the Quanta $35M strategic injection; the large cash position relative to burn rate implies a runway exceeding four years at current spending levels absent acceleration.

GAAP P&L is significantly distorted by non-cash derivative liabilities from the 2022 SPAC transaction: Q4 2024 GAAP net loss was $153.0M (including $135.1M in warrant/earn-out fair-value changes) while non-GAAP loss was far smaller; Q1 2026 showed GAAP net income of $33.1M entirely due to $62.1M of non-cash gains from derivative warrant and earn-out liabilities, masking a $14.7M non-GAAP operating loss; analysts must strip these items for operational analysis.

Comparable peers trade at similar speculative multiples: IonQ (NASDAQ: IONQ, FY2025 revenue $130M, market cap ~$8B range) and D-Wave Quantum (NASDAQ: QBTS) are the closest listed comparables; Quantinuum (private, Honeywell-backed) and PsiQuantum (private) are unlisted; IBM and Google quantum divisions are not ring-fenced, making direct comp impossible; Rigetti's $8.79B market cap on $7.1M trailing revenue is at the extreme end of the speculative tech spectrum.

Market cap volatility has been extreme: RGTI market capitalization rose from approximately $441.6M in January 2025 to $7.32B by December 2025 — a 1,555% gain — before moderating and then recovering to approximately $8.79B by May 2026; shares outstanding increased 47.6% year-over-year to 332.4M, reflecting continuous dilution from ATM offerings and warrant exercises; the stock's high beta relative to the NASDAQ makes financial projections highly sensitive to sentiment shifts in the quantum computing sector.

leadership.key_finding: Rigetti Computing's leadership team is a semiconductor-and-sensors industry transplant, not a quantum physics native, which is a deliberate choice by the board following the post-SPAC governance reset. CEO Dr. Subodh Kulkarni — appointed December 2022 — brings thirty-plus years of scaling and commercializing cutting-edge hardware technologies in the semiconductor supply chain. His terminal role before Rigetti was President and CEO of CyberOptics Corporation, a precision sensor company that he guided to a successful trade sale to Nordson Corporation in November 2022 at what investors viewed as an attractive exit multiple. CFO Jeffrey Bertelsen joined in February 2023, was also a CyberOptics veteran (CFO and COO from 2005 to 2022), meaning the two top operational executives shared years of prior institutional collaboration — reducing execution friction during the critical 2023-2025 commercialization build-out. CTO David Rivas, appointed February 2023, provides the technical counterbalance on the executive team. Board governance underwent its own reset: Thomas J.
